page: The Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-800s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor family. It features 4 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16 alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. The server does not include a GPU accelerator.

Memory architecture is a primary attribute of this configuration, supplying 32 GB of system RAM at an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, which places the platform into memory-optimized territory. Primary local storage is delivered via an integrated 800 GB NVMe SSD, providing low-latency disk throughput alongside one complimentary public IPv4 network address.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate exceptional single-core compute throughput, with stress-ng single-core tests ranking in the top ten percent. Large block uncached memory write throughput is strong at 115.6 GB/sec, complemented by strong single-threaded gzip and bzip3 execution speeds. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics reflect the two physical core constraint, yielding average multi-core Geekbench and stress-ng scores. PassMark database tests, static web serving throughput, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression register in the lower percentiles, while medium-sized language model inference remains constrained by compute core limits.

The instance offers solid resource efficiency for memory-bound applications without forcing the provisioning of redundant CPU cores. Its combination of dedicated AMD EPYC processing, 32 GB memory capacity, and fast local NVMe storage fits in-memory caching solutions such as Redis, text processing engines, extract-transform-load tasks, and memory-intensive backend services.
